title: Office and Facilities Manager
description:
Grade: NJC Point 31 - £43,149 per annum
Hours: Full-time - 37.5 hours per week (excluding breaks)
Contract: Permanent (subject to the successful completion of a 3-month probationary period)
Days: Monday to Friday during our core hours, in person in our busy office

This is an exciting opportunity to take on a key role at the heart of Salford CVS. As our full-time Office and Facilities Manager, you will make sure our premises, systems and services run smoothly for our staff, members and visitors. You will be leading a team of three administrators and a caretaker/facilities worker.

Main purposes of the post

The Office and Facilities Manager will manage wide-ranging administrative and operational support to ensure an efficient office environment, provide excellent services to our members and the wider team, contributing directly to the delivery of Salford CVS's priorities. You will also actively manage our physical premises. The postholder will act as Salford CVS's Data Protection Lead (supported by an external data protection consultant) and Health and Safety Officer, and will be the main point of contact for IT, leading on cyber security and compliance. The Office and Facilities Manager will be responsible for four members of staff.

Benefits
- 28 days' holiday - rising to 30 days (after five years), plus Bank Holidays (pro rata for part-time)
- Enhanced company sick and maternity pay, subject to terms and conditions of service
- Pension scheme - with 7% employer contribution (and 1% mandatory employee contribution)
- Cycle to Work scheme
- Membership of the Hospital Saturday Fund via an employer subsidised scheme (optional and non-contractual)
- RHS family membership (optional and non-contractual)
- Development opportunities - we support and encourage our staff to progress in their careers (including formal training)
- A supportive working culture - we respect and support one another to do the best we can

We are an accredited Living Wage Employer, Living Hours Employer and Living Wage Funder, ensuring not just our staff are paid the 'real' Living Wage but also that any projects we fund can do the same.

For further information and to apply, please visit our website via the 'apply' button.

Closing date: 12 Noon on Wednesday 11th November 2026.

Interviews will take place in person at Salford CVS' offices in Eccles on Tuesday 24th November 2026.

title: Human Resources and Organisational Development Manager
description:

Hours: Full-time - 37.5 hours per week (excluding breaks)

As the organisation continues to grow and develop, we are strengthening the way we recruit, develop, support and look after our people.

We are now looking to appoint an experienced Human Resources and Organisational Development Manager to lead our human resources function and drive organisational development across Salford CVS. This is a key role, working closely with the Chief Executive and Senior Management Team.

You will be a knowledgeable, approachable and highly organised HR professional, confident in leading across the full range of people matters, developing our staff and leaders, and helping to keep the organisation compliant.

To lead on training, learning and organisational development, and to support effective HR compliance (including the active management of up-to-date HR policies and procedures), helping Salford CVS to be a well-run, inclusive and high-performing organisation.

title: Recruitment Coordinator
description:
About Tutor Trust

We're a proudly Northern charity that believes in equity in education. We do our bit to achieve that by partnering with schools and education providers, to enable their young people to work alongside inspiring and motivating tutors - an opportunity they may not otherwise have.

We know that our high-quality tuition helps improve young people's academic attainment, wellbeing, and self-confidence, and supports their personal aspirations.

The NTP which ran from 2020 to 2024 allowed us to reach more pupils than ever before. However, the end of NTP subsidies and other pressures on school budgets mean we are increasingly relying on fundraising, projects etc to enable us to continue to support a high number of pupils.

Our values

What we stand for and practise in everything we do at Tutor Trust:

We believe in fairness

We are passionate about making a difference

We are inclusive and supportive

We are quality-focused

We are ambitious

We learn

Benefits of working at Tutor Trust

Hybrid work model (2 days in the office)

Competitive leave - 33 days per annum (inclusive of Bank Holidays, pro rata)

Flexible working including Time Off In Lieu (TOIL)

Health and Wellbeing (Employee Assistance Programme, 24-hour GP service, mental health support and benefits platform, Perkbox)

Enhanced Family and Sick Leave (after a qualifying period).

Recognition and Culture (Thanks & Recognition, Highlights, team events)

Learning and Development (knowledge sharing, staff-led groups)

Job Purpose:

The role of Recruitment Coordinator will involve the administration of safer recruitment checks and the onboarding of new tutors. Alongside this, you'll handle the wider admin that keeps tutor recruitment moving: recruitment correspondence, enquiries from candidates, and keeping our Applicant Tracking System and Single Central Record up to date. You will assist the Recruitment Team in ensuring that the tutor recruitment process runs smoothly and effectively across all city regions that we work with. This role is Manchester-based but will cover recruitment over all Tutor Trust locations.

Job Responsibilities:

Safer recruitment

Administer safer recruitment checks for all tutors, including approving references, processing enhanced DBS checks, and overseeing Update Service renewals.

Maintain accurate records of safer recruitment checks for all tutors.

Ensure adherence to safer recruitment practices throughout the recruitment process.

Tutor recruitment & development processes

Update and maintain accurate records on the Tutor Application Tracking System and Single Central Record (SCR) along with other tracking of candidates.

Support with day-to-day administration and engagement of tutor trainees, including monitoring and supporting their progression.

Assist with all tutor interviews, training and tutor L&D events, which are currently taking place online. This includes acting as an Interview Coordinator during interviews, interviewing candidates, collecting and recording evidence of identification documents, and ensuring that interviews and other events run smoothly.

Assist with the complete recruitment process for tutors, including shortlisting, interviewing, and onboarding, alongside other members of the Recruitment & Development Team.

Administrative support

Provide administrative support to the R&D Team, including managing recruitment correspondence and data entry.

Support the tracking and analysis of recruitment data, to assist with the production of reports.

Respond to recruitment and training enquiries via email and phone, alongside other members of the Tutor Recruitment & Development team.

Assist with general office functions.

Safeguarding & Compliance
- Contribute to the monitoring and reporting of all safeguarding concern processes, within your teams, ensuring all concerns are reported promptly to the Designated Safeguarding Lead or deputies, and helping to promote and foster a culture of vigilance and accountability across The Tutor Trust.Take responsibility for monitoring safeguarding processes within your teams.

General Duties

Collaborate with colleagues across teams and regions to ensure consistent messaging and effective communication.

Assist other staff to complete a variety of tasks that enable the Trust to operate effectively and efficiently.

Any other duties commensurate with the grade and nature of the post.

Person Specification

Strong candidates for this role will demonstrate a solid track record of performance, possess excellent IT and English skills, exhibit strong interpersonal and diplomatic abilities, and show initiative in their approach.

Skills

Communication & Interpersonal Skills

Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to build rapport with stakeholders at all levels and across sectors.

Confident in representing the organisation in meetings, presentations, and events.

Organisational & Time Management

Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines effectively.

Ability to work under pressure while maintaining consistently high standards of work.

Administrative and IT Skills

Proven administrative experience in a previous paid or voluntary role.

Fully IT literate, with particular competence in Microsoft Excel and Access.

Ability to manage office systems, databases, and documentation accurately and efficiently.

Independent and Team Working Skills

Able to work collaboratively as part of a team and independently when required.

Quick to grasp new concepts and adapt to changing priorities.

Attributes

Committed to safeguarding children and young people, and willing to undergo DBS clearance.

Alignment with the goals, ethos, and mission of the Tutor Trust.

Empathy for disadvantaged and vulnerable learners.

Enthusiastic and proactive in contributing to organisational growth and success.

Excellent time-management and attention to detail.

Strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative working style.

Willingness to work outside standard hours when required.

General

How to apply

To apply, download an application form, an equality and diversity monitoring form and send your completed documents to the email address provided.

The role is based on a fixed-term basis from 4th January to 30th June 2027. Your regular place of work will be the Tutor Trust Head Office in Manchester; however, the position will also involve occasional travel to our partners.

The hours of work are 36.25 hours per week over 52 weeks (hybrid working currently in operation). Holiday entitlement will be 33 days per annum (inclusive of Bank Holidays). There may also involve working occasional unsocial hours in evenings.

The Tutor Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people in line with Keeping Children Safe in Education. We expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. All appointments are subject to safer recruitment procedures, including an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check, satisfactory references, and verification of the right to work in the UK.

The Tutor Trust is an Equal Opportunities Employer. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are committed to fair treatment throughout the recruitment process and beyond.

We believe that a diverse team drives innovation and strengthens the programmes we deliver to pupils. Diversity spans many dimensions of identity, and we are committed to cultivating an inclusive, equitable workplace where every voice is heard, respected, and valued.

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: To be first point of contact for the visitors of the Education Campus while manning reception areas and completing admin tasks, such as actioning room booking requests, inputting data and creating daily documents to insure the smooth running of the Education Campus. The post-holder will work as part of the Education Campus team based on the Oxford Road Campus (near Manchester Royal Infirmary). The post holder's main role will act as the Receptionist and will be the first point of contact for all users, patients and visitors to the Education Campus. The post holder will also assist in providing administrative support to the Education Campus team and assist with the processing of all room requests via the electronic booking system. The post holder will also receive deliveries, report maintenance issues and help with the daily monitoring of room usage and signing in process. IMPORTANT CANDIDATE INFORMATION To find out more about the key responsibilities and the specific skills and experience youll need for this role, take a look at the Job Description & Person Specification attachments under the Documents to download heading. Explore Inside MFT Your Candidate Place To help you feel confident, prepared and fully informed before you apply, we invite you to explore Inside MFT Your Candidate Place . This welcoming onestop hub gives you a real sense of who we are, what we stand for, how we reward and support you, and the many ways we care for you as you care for others. Youll also find practical hints and tips for submitting a great application, along with the essential information you need to know before you apply. To access Inside MFT Your Candidate Place , simply click on the relevant PDF document under the Documents to download heading and once opened, you can either scan QR code or click on the link provided. Closing vacancy listings early We welcome applications from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences.To help us manage applications fairly and give each one the time it deserves, our adverts may close early if we receive a high level of interest. Early applications are therefore encouraged. Diversity Matters MFT is committed to promoting equality of opportunity, celebrating and valuing diversity and eliminating any form of unlawful discrimination across our workforce, ensuring our people are truly representative of the communities we serve. All individuals regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation are encouraged to apply for this post. As an inclusive employer, we are here to support you. If you have any special requirements to help you with your application, please contact the manager named below. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in your application Here at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust, were proud to be ALL HERE FOR YOU, for our patients, our communities, and each other.As part of our commitment to fairness, transparency, and personal integrity, we ask all applicants to ensure that their job applications reflect their own experiences, skills, and motivations. While AI tools can support spelling, grammar, or formatting, we expect that the content of your application, especially personal statements and responses to role specific questions is written by you. This helps us get to know the real you and ensures that our recruitment process remains equitable and meaningful for everyone. Thank you for helping us uphold the values that make our Trust a place where people belong, grow, and thrive. We look forward to receiving your application. Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check As part of our commitment to safeguarding patients and staff, many roles at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) require a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. This is a standard process across the NHS and helps us ensure a safe environment for everyone. What is a DBS Check? A DBS check is a background check that reveals any criminal convictions, cautions, reprimands, or warnings. The level of check required depends on the role: Standard DBS : Checks for spent and unspent convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings. Enhanced DBS : Includes the above, plus any additional information held by local police thats considered relevant to the role. Enhanced with Barred Lists: Includes all of the above, plus checks against the childrens and/or adults barred lists. Who Needs a DBS Check Most roles involving direct patient contact, working with children or vulnerable adults, or access to sensitive information will require a DBS check. The job advert and recruitment team will let you know if this applies to your role. The Costs for a DBS At Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT), roles that require a DBS check are subject to a cost recovery policy. This means that the cost of submitting and processing a DBS application if you are successful and join us, will be deducted from your salary within the first three months of employment. If, however, you withdraw from a conditional offer after the DBS process has begun, you will still be liable for the cost incurred. For more information about the cost of the various types of DBS, please visit: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/dbs-fees-are-changing-in-december DBS Update Service Candidates are also expected to register with the DBS Update Service which must be completed within 30 days of the certificate being issued. This helps streamline future employment checks and supports safer recruitment practices. For more information, please visit the DBS Update Service.
